a_raw: {"translation":"Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every type X, every type Y, every function f from finite lists of X to Y, and every natural number T, there exists a single N of type S1 X Y satisfying three conditions. First, its dependency relation has no directed cycle of positive length, including a self-loop. There is an edge from m to n if there exist two full states that agree at every index other than m and an input x for which the update of n gives different values in those two states. The states in this test need not be reachable. Second, N has exactly T state indices; this counts indices, not the possible values at each index, whose types need not be finite. Third, for every list xs of elements of X of length at most T, the output of N equals f(xs): N starts in its specified initial state, processes xs from left to right by updating all indices from the previous full state and the current input, and applies its output function to the final state. The same N must work for all such lists, including the empty list, but no agreement with f is required on longer lists. T may be zero, in which case N must have no indices and agreement is required only on the empty list."}
translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every type X, every type Y, every function f from finite lists of X to Y, and every natural number T, there exists a single N of type S1 X Y satisfying three conditions. First, its dependency relation has no directed cycle of positive length, including a self-loop. There is an edge from m to n if there exist two full states that agree at every index other than m and an input x for which the update of n gives different values in those two states. The states in this test need not be reachable. Second, N has exactly T state indices; this counts indices, not the possible values at each index, whose types need not be finite. Third, for every list xs of elements of X of length at most T, the output of N equals f(xs): N starts in its specified initial state, processes xs from left to right by updating all indices from the previous full state and the current input, and applies its output function to the final state. The same N must work for all such lists, including the empty list, but no agreement with f is required on longer lists. T may be zero, in which case N must have no indices and agreement is required only on the empty list.

judgement.summary: The TARGET defines, without proving, exactly the stated claim: one loop-free system with exactly T state indices must agree with f on every list of length at most T. Doerig et al. speak of approximation with finitely many neurons but give no specific count; Herzog et al. speak of implementing functions even when time matters.
